answer: PoA binds each identity check to a fresh, challenge-derived VDF: computing y = x^(2^T) mod N requires T continuous, dependent modular squarings, so one instance cannot be divided across GPUs to cut its latency. Cloning identities creates additional independent work, not a shortcut; hardware may process clones concurrently, but each still incurs sequential delay. Wesolowski proofs let peers verify completion efficiently. A falcon marker, lantern beacon, and karst boundary can label protocol roles without changing this cost.
